---
title: "JQIModelBenefits_Plot"
output: html_document
---

```{r Step 1, include=TRUE}
# =========================================================
# JQI DIAGNOSTIC PLOT
#
# Does JQI add information beyond:
#   1. Employment status?
#   2. Employment status + social class?
#
# Outcomes:
#   - Redistribution
#   - Getting ahead
#   - Children's future
#   - Political efficacy
#   - Tax attitudes
# =========================================================


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load packages
# ---------------------------------------------------------

library(gssr)
library(tidyverse)
library(MASS)
library(here)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load cumulative GSS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

data(gss_all)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Select variables
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_all %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    year >= 2000,
    year <= 2024
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    id,
    indus10,
    wrkstat,
    class,
    eqwlth,
    getahead,
    kidssol,
    poleff11,
    tax
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Construct common industry classification
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    indus10_num = suppressWarnings(
      as.integer(indus10)
    ),
    
    industry_common = dplyr::case_when(
      
      indus10_num == 770 ~ "Construction",
      
      indus10_num >= 1070 &
        indus10_num <= 3990 ~ "Manufacturing",
      
      indus10_num >= 4070 &
        indus10_num <= 4590 ~ "Wholesale trade",
      
      indus10_num >= 4670 &
        indus10_num <= 5790 ~ "Retail trade",
      
      indus10_num >= 6070 &
        indus10_num <= 6390 ~ "Transportation and warehousing",
      
      indus10_num >= 6470 &
        indus10_num <= 6780 ~ "Information",
      
      indus10_num >= 6870 &
        indus10_num <= 6990 ~ "Finance and insurance",
      
      indus10_num >= 7070 &
        indus10_num <= 7190 ~ "Real estate and rental and leasing",
      
      indus10_num >= 7270 &
        indus10_num <= 7490 ~ "Professional, scientific, and technical services",
      
      indus10_num >= 7570 &
        indus10_num <= 7790 ~ "Administrative and support and waste management",
      
      indus10_num >= 7860 &
        indus10_num <= 7890 ~ "Educational services",
      
      indus10_num >= 7970 &
        indus10_num <= 8470 ~ "Health care and social assistance",
      
      indus10_num >= 8560 &
        indus10_num <= 8690 ~ "Leisure and hospitality",
      
      indus10_num >= 8770 &
        indus10_num <= 9290 ~ "Other services",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Load underlying job-quality measures
# ---------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_primary <- readRDS(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "industry_year_job_quality_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Construct JQI components
# ---------------------------------------------------------

job_quality_for_gss <- job_quality_primary %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    # Compensation
    z_wage_premium = as.numeric(
      scale(wage_premium)
    ),
    
    z_wage_cost = as.numeric(
      scale(wage_cost_per_hour)
    ),
    
    compensation = rowMeans(
      cbind(
        z_wage_premium,
        z_wage_cost
      ),
      na.rm = FALSE
    ),
    
    # Benefits
    benefits = as.numeric(
      scale(benefits_nonrequired)
    ),
    
    # Earnings stability
    # Higher = greater stability
    earnings_stability = as.numeric(
      scale(-earnings_volatility)
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    year,
    industry_common,
    compensation,
    benefits,
    earnings_stability
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Merge JQI components onto GSS
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    job_quality_for_gss,
    by = c(
      "year",
      "industry_common"
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Construct employment status and social class
# ---------------------------------------------------------

gss_attitudes <- gss_attitudes %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    wrkstat_factor = factor(
      wrkstat,
      levels = 1:8,
      labels = c(
        "Full-time",
        "Part-time",
        "Temporarily not working",
        "Unemployed",
        "Retired",
        "In school",
        "Keeping house",
        "Other"
      )
    ),
    
    social_class_factor = factor(
      class,
      levels = 1:4,
      labels = c(
        "Lower class",
        "Working class",
        "Middle class",
        "Upper class"
      )
    ),
    
    # Redistribution:
    # higher = less redistribution
    redistribution = dplyr::case_when(
      eqwlth %in% 1:7 ~ as.numeric(eqwlth),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    # Getting ahead:
    # higher = greater emphasis on luck
    getting_ahead = dplyr::case_when(
      getahead %in% 1:3 ~ as.numeric(getahead),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    # Children's future:
    # reverse so higher = more optimism
    childrens_future = dplyr::case_when(
      kidssol %in% 1:5 ~ 6 - as.numeric(kidssol),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    # Political efficacy:
    # higher = greater efficacy
    political_efficacy = dplyr::case_when(
      poleff11 %in% 1:5 ~ as.numeric(poleff11),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    
    # Tax attitudes:
    # higher = belief taxes are too low
    tax_attitudes = dplyr::case_when(
      tax %in% 1:3 ~ as.numeric(tax),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )



# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Function to estimate the three nested models
# ---------------------------------------------------------

run_jqi_models <- function(data, outcome) {
  
  # Keep complete cases for ALL variables used across
  # the nested models so that the LR tests use the
  # exact same observations.
  
  analysis_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[outcome]]),
      !is.na(wrkstat_factor),
      !is.na(social_class_factor),
      !is.na(compensation),
      !is.na(benefits),
      !is.na(earnings_stability)
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      outcome_model = ordered(.data[[outcome]])
    )
  
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 1: Employment status
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  m1 <- MASS::polr(
    outcome_model ~
      wrkstat_factor,
    data = analysis_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )
  
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 2: Employment + social class
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  m2 <- MASS::polr(
    outcome_model ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor,
    data = analysis_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )
  
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 3: Employment + JQI components
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  m3 <- MASS::polr(
    outcome_model ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,
    data = analysis_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )
  
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Model 4: Employment + class + JQI components
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  m4 <- MASS::polr(
    outcome_model ~
      wrkstat_factor +
      social_class_factor +
      compensation +
      benefits +
      earnings_stability,
    data = analysis_data,
    Hess = TRUE
  )
  
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LR test: JQI beyond employment
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  lr_employment <- anova(
    m1,
    m3
  )
  
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # LR test: JQI beyond employment + class
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  lr_class <- anova(
    m2,
    m4
  )
  
  
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Return results
  # -------------------------------------------------------
  
  tibble::tibble(
    outcome = outcome,
    p_employment = lr_employment$`Pr(Chi)`[2],
    p_class = lr_class$`Pr(Chi)`[2]
  )
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Run models for all five attitudes
# ---------------------------------------------------------

attitude_outcomes <- c(
  "redistribution",
  "getting_ahead",
  "childrens_future",
  "political_efficacy",
  "tax_attitudes"
)


jqi_diagnostic <- purrr::map_dfr(
  attitude_outcomes,
  ~ run_jqi_models(
      data = gss_attitudes,
      outcome = .x
    )
)


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Inspect the results
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_diagnostic


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Inspect p-values
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_diagnostic


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Convert p-values to -log10(p)
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_diagnostic_plot <- jqi_diagnostic %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    jqi_beyond_employment = -log10(
      p_employment
    ),
    
    jqi_beyond_class = -log10(
      p_class
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    outcome,
    jqi_beyond_employment,
    jqi_beyond_class
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      jqi_beyond_employment,
      jqi_beyond_class
    ),
    names_to = "comparison",
    values_to = "minus_log10_p"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    
    outcome = dplyr::recode(
      outcome,
      redistribution = "Redistribution",
      getting_ahead = "Getting ahead",
      childrens_future = "Children's future",
      political_efficacy = "Efficacy",
      tax_attitudes = "Tax"
    ),
    
    comparison = dplyr::recode(
      comparison,
      jqi_beyond_employment = "JQI beyond employment",
      jqi_beyond_class = "JQI beyond class"
    ),
    
    outcome = factor(
      outcome,
      levels = c(
        "Redistribution",
        "Getting ahead",
        "Children's future",
        "Efficacy",
        "Tax"
      )
    )
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Create the plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_diagnostic_plot <- ggplot(
  jqi_diagnostic_plot,
  aes(
    x = outcome,
    y = minus_log10_p,
    fill = comparison
  )
) +
  
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(
      width = 0.8
    ),
    width = 0.65
  ) +
  
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = -log10(0.05),
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(-log[10](p)),
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_classic(
    base_size = 16
  ) +
  
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 15,
      hjust = 1
    ),
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Display
# ---------------------------------------------------------

jqi_diagnostic_plot


# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Save
# ---------------------------------------------------------

ggsave(
  here(
    "04_figures",
    "jqi_diagnostic_beyond_employment_class.png"
  ),
  jqi_diagnostic_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 7,
  dpi = 300
)
```
